The loneliest peptide party in Fresh York

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1984 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: The Verge

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The peptide curious are looking for answers, and finding dubious products instead.﻿.
  • This is Optimizer, a weekly newsletter sent from Verge senior reviewer Victoria Song that dissects and discusses the latest gizmos and potions that swear they’re going to change your life.
  • On a rainy fall evening, an experimental art venue in Chelsea Market had a small line out the door.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The peptide curious are looking for answers, and finding dubious products instead.﻿.

Photography by Jack Califano / The Verge.

This is Optimizer, a weekly newsletter sent from Verge senior reviewer Victoria Song that dissects and discusses the latest gizmos and potions that swear they’re going to change your life. Opt in for Optimizer here.

On a rainy fall evening, an experimental art venue in Chelsea Market had a small line out the door. There are always lines in Fresh York City. Viral food trends, gallery exhibitions, pop-ups, and parties. The folks in line looked like your average joe, ready for a Friday night on the town. You wouldn’t look twice — except, perhaps, for a man with a wizard beard and a laser sword strapped to his back.

Inside, the man with a laser sword stood in the middle of the cavernous bottom floor of a two-story warehouse strewn with large bean bags. On the wall were psychedelic projections of jellyfish, shrimp, and other sea creatures. A bizarre choice, considering peptides won’t induce any trippy vision quests, and not a single person was getting groovy. The industrial beams had posters with QR codes that you could scan to get samples of Afterglow, a new type of peptide product. According to seemingly discarded pamphlets around the venue, Afterglow isn’t a standard injectable or oral peptide. The firm makes strips that dissolve under the tongue. The “Afterglow Peptide Field Guide” also described what each sample does, dosing recommendations, and potential side effects. At the upstairs bar, bartenders mixed custom cocktails called Afterburn — complete with bioluminescent veggie nectar — and Margatrutide. (For the record, a bioluminescent veggie nectar cocktail tastes as awful as you think.).

Welcome to a peptide launch party.

Peptide parties are old news in San Francisco, but they’re somewhat more novel in Newly introduced York City. Milling around the edges of the venue were various reporters and photographers. We were all trying to get a sense of why anyone had bothered to come out. Not that many did. Despite the venue’s size, the main floor had plenty of empty space.

One person I spoke to was a fencer with sore joints. They’d heard that one of the peptides might help with recovery. Another had a father in the wellness industry and had heard vague things about how effective peptides could be. One woman, staring at a projected jellyfish, merely shrugged. Her friend was more into “wellness stuff” and she had no looks, so, why not check out a party? A man, staring into his bag of Afterglow samples, was mostly interested in weight loss but scared about the safety of gray market products. A few feet away, another man was furiously reading the Afterglow pamphlet. “I like to know what I put in my body,” he stated.

The only problem was he didn’t remember which sample he had tried.

Sources indicate that A common refrain: Well, this beats doing research online. This, at least, was a social event where you could theoretically connect with other people. And there were clusters of strangers speaking to each other. Mostly, near the bar. Everywhere else, people stared awkwardly on their phones, their eyes occasionally roaming the room without meeting anyone else’s gaze for more than a second or two. After a while, they’d disappear into the back room and reappear with a goody bag full of peptide samples.

Industry observers note that after 90 minutes, I decided to leave. For the umpteenth time that evening, I’d walked up to someone, asked about peptides, and got a noncommittal “I really don’t know anything — I just came to learn more.” (When asked if they had, they invariably shrugged and pointed to the goody bag.) It was clear that the only peptide evangelists here were likely associated with the launch. The whole thing, to me, seemed as if someone had tried to draw a cool party from memory. The last thing I saw was a person draped in a ghost sheet sitting alone in the corner.

Recent findings suggest that as it turned out, the man with the laser sword was a performance artist who’d been invited to attend. Out of journalistic integrity, I asked if he had ever tried peptides. He told me he was more interested in the unifying energy of the universe. When I got up to leave, he waved and stated, “Giggles.”.

According to recent reports, if I were peptide curious, the Afterglow launch party was a pretty awful way to learn anything about these substances. To be fair, Afterglow’s Partiful invitation mostly described this event as “an environment great for aura farming” and the “hard launch of [its] first of many experiments in culture.” Nevertheless, as part of the press, I did walk away with a smattering of Afterglow’s products. In total, I got packets of what Afterglow calls Charge (NAD+), Rejuvenate (glutathione), Wolverine Blend (BPC-157 / TB-500), Strength Blend (CJC-1295 / Ipamorelin), Glow Blend (GHK-Cu / BPC-157 / TB-500), Connect (PT-141), GLP-2 (tirzepatide), and GLP-3 (retatrutide). Or at least that’s what the packaging states. There’s no way to truly verify gray market peptides for safety or efficacy because they’re unregulated products.

According to recent reports, first of all, last I checked, GLP-1 medications do not upgrade like iPhone models. Afterglow’s pamphlet correctly lists that your body has “three hormone switches”: GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon. The accompanying descriptors of what each does are broadly correct, though lacking in nuance. For example, there is a hormone called glucagon-like peptide 2, but it’s not tirzepatide. The “real” GLP-2 is a hormone related to intestinal health. Tirzepatide is still considered a GLP-1 medication that’s a dual agonist because it works on two hormones (GLP-1 and GIP.) The GLP-2 moniker is a misnomer popularized by ill-informed influencers. The same goes for retatrutide, which, as of this writing, is still an unapproved GLP-1 medication that works on three hormones (GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon) and is therefore a triple agonist. There is no such thing as GLP-3.

Recent findings suggest that for all the samples, there were no instructions regarding dosing on the packaging — just another QR code leading to Afterglow’s product page. Those pages happen to contain instructions for how to use the strips, and the amount of product within the strips. There are disclaimers about how little studied the compounds are, but nothing about interactions, side effects, or what to expect while taking. Just a throwaway line to talk to your doctor.

All that information, you’d have to find on the pamphlet given at the party. (Ironically, some “vital cautions” on the pamphlet state to avoid taking samples with alcohol, at a party where the booze was flowing.) Provided you didn’t throw it out. One would hope that information is on a box if you were to buy directly from the seller. But for all intents and purposes, what I just described is what a clueless partygoer would have to go on.

If everything in that pamphlet were 100 percent factual, perhaps a conscientious partygoer could feel reassured. On that front, I have bad news. The pamphlet calls PT-141 an “FDA-approved peptide that boosts sexual desire for both men and women.”.

Industry observers note that PT-141, also known as bremelanotide or Vyleesi, is FDA approved. But only for premenopausal women suffering from hypoactive sexual desire disorder. It is not approved for post-menopausal women, men, or for general sexual performance enhancement.

In a recent development, another concern: How does one evaluate a sublingual peptide strip? Specifically, is this delivery method even scientifically proven effective in humans? Spoiler: It’s not! A collapsible FAQ menu on Afterglow’s site states, “We don’t know yet. Nobody has published how much of most peptides reaches the blood from a strip compared with an injection. We’re funding studies to measure exactly that, and we’ll share what we find.”.

In a recent development, as for why you’d want to even try a sublingual strip? Afterglow’s website suggests it’s more convenient than injections or pills. No refrigeration, no needles, and no need for learning how to reconstitute a drug. Just pop a strip under the tongue and go.

And good luck trying to find reputable sources of information on your own. Afterglow states it’s funding its own research, but its site has no reviewable documentation just yet. A Google search brings up a questionable AI overview, a handful of links from dubious med spas, a couple of dead links, and one PubMed study in mice. Most of the links also primarily discuss the difference between oral peptides in pill form and injectables — so not terribly relevant here.

Recent findings suggest that I’d consider it fair game if I were confident that anyone at the party I went to did their due diligence. As it stands, I talked with over a dozen people who were mostly there for vibes, booze, and freebies.

Not all peptide parties are created equal. Some happen on WWII cargo ships, complete with panel discussions about peptide supply chains. Another “peptide 101” talk I attended in New York happened at the back of a bitcoin bar. There, most attendees also knew very little about peptides, but at least they got treated to a PowerPoint presentation about the basics. There was a dubious demonstration of how to inject oneself that would’ve probably made any pharmacist or doctor scream. But at the very least, peptides were defined and attendees could ask questions. (The answers to those questions were on the right track with regard to the dangers of the gray market. They were less reliable about scientific rigor and why “anecdotal evidence” is not the same as clinical evidence of safety.).

It has been revealed that but a striking, recurring theme is just how much is unknown. These substances aren’t well-studied in humans, so there’s not much evidence as to long-term benefits or side effects. The peptide curious know shocking little about the substances they’re supposedly interested in. Likewise, it’s incredibly difficult to get reliable, unbiased data on gray market interest or usage, though there have been attempts to quantify this surging demand in recent months. Case in point, telehealth provider Hims & Hers just conducted a consumer survey of roughly 2,000 American adults. Of those surveyed, 68 percent remarked they had little to no knowledge about peptides. Less than 18 percent were even able to identify that peptides are chains of amino acids. Even so, 40 percent said they were interested or very interested in trying injectable prescription treatments — including peptides — if offered by a telehealth service.

It has been revealed that even so, peptides are everywhere. The word appears in copious ads for skincare creams, weight loss drugs, and supplements. Looksmaxxers, influencers, and celebrities like Gwyneth Paltrow and Joe Rogan talk about them in podcasts, documentaries, and social media as if they’re miracle shortcuts. Hims & Hers has even confirmed it’s launching a service called Peptide Plus — nevermind that the vast majority of what it’ll offer are not actual peptides.

It has been revealed that in this kind of environment, of course more people will become peptide curious. Which makes it even more concerning that the most readily available information sources are not medical or scientific experts well-versed on the topic at hand. There are dubious links online summarized into less-than-critical AI overviews. There are pamphlets handed out at weird parties, where there’s more booze and schmooze than education. Influencers branding themselves as experts as they flash crudely summarized studies in a bar back room. Industry panels that are inaccessible to the average consumer, full of jargon and assumed knowledge of the science at hand.

According to recent reports, it’s clear something needs to be done until general knowledge improves. Until then, the parties will continue.

Huang used the moment to say that his interests align with the US’s, saying:.

It has been revealed that I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. Nvidia has been my life’s work. Building it into the manufacturer it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like Nvidia be possible. I love our country, and I love Nvidia.

Trump may have learned as early as this spring that Huang was potentially the target of Chinese espionage, but the president claimed recently that he didn’t know Huang was potentially exposed to a Chinese spy as he was becoming a prominent part of Trump’s inner circle, CNN reported.

If Trump wasn’t adequately briefed, it raises question about whether the White House acted with “sufficient urgency” to address a serious espionage threat, CNN said. But if Trump is deflecting, an even “graver question” will emerge about why Trump didn’t act on information and instead continued to keep Huang close, CNN said.

Instead of distancing himself from the Nvidia CEO, Trump invited Huang to sit at the head table during a state dinner with China’s president Xi Jinping, and last month, Trump awarded Huang the National Medal of Science, the nation’s highest scientiﬁc honor, for his AI achievements.

In a recent development, “Not only has he continued to do nothing, he’s invited that very CEO into the White House and on state visits to China with him,” Sacha Haworth, TOP’s founder and CEO, told Ars. “And the question we all have to ask is ‘why on Earth would he do that?’”.

Recent findings suggest that what Trump and Nvidia knew—and when—have become central questions for some Republicans, as well as top Democrats who strategy to investigate the scandal when they assume control of key committees in Congress next year. Andrew Yoon, head of research for a nonprofit called CivAI, which warns the public of dangers from AI, told Ars that Huang doesn’t need to be compromised by China to have endangered the US. Prioritizing boosting profits over national security alone is “pretty concerning.”.

Sources indicate that “I think the most notable thing here is that Jensen Huang has been at the absolute forefront of lobbying to be able to sell chips to China,” Yoon remarked. “He has leveraged his very deep relationships with government, especially President Trump, in order to be able to sell as many Nvidia chips to China as he can get away with. If he could be selling Blackwell chips to China, I’m sure he would be.”.

Industry observers note that yoon noted that evidence suggests some Chinese AI models have been trained on Blackwell chips. Even with China’s push to prioritize domestic chipmakers like Huawei, Nvidia chips remain “indispensable” to China’s frontier AI goals, Yoon noted. And national security experts fear that access to high-end chips will help China advance its military AI or gain economic ground.

It has been revealed that the White House isn’t commenting on Trump’s relationship with Huang. Among the lawmakers accusing the Trump administration of “corruption” is Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), The Wall Street Journal reported. He has already asked the White House to “preserve all communications” between Trump and Huang.

It has been revealed that other lawmakers are “seeking more information about what Trump knew about the relationship between Jensen Huang and Alice Huang,” the former Megaspeed CEO whom Huang admitted to having an affair with. They also want to know more about “the administration’s failure to stop artiﬁcial-intelligence chips from going to China,” WSJ reported, and Nvidia’s reportedly $25 million donation to the White House ballroom.

In a recent development, “It is not just an intelligence issue; it’s also a potential corruption issue,” Blumenthal said. “There needs to be a really penetrating, comprehensive investigation of all the possible compromises of our intelligence that may have occurred, but also… that Donald Trump is so high on the head of Nvidia, and now is potentially linked to intelligence compromises.”.

In a recent development, trump has profited off Nvidia’s success while in office, buying “millions of dollars worth of Nvidia shares in his personal brokerage accounts since returning to oﬃce in 2025,” the WSJ reported. The White House maintains that the president has no role in managing his stock portfolio.

Industry observers note that other officials advising Trump on AI also benefited from relaxing export curbs, TOP remarked. On Tuesday, the group issued a report summarizing what the public knows about potential conflicts of interest of two Trump officials: former White House AI Czar David Sacks and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.

Haworth, TOP’s founder, told Ars she’s concerned that Sacks and Lutnick abused their power to convince Trump to let Nvidia sell cutting-edge technology to China, while standing to “gain astronomical amounts of money.”.

“The public is outraged by Nvidia’s CEO for compromising our national security, but we didn’t get here because of Jensen Huang’s missteps alone,” Haworth noted. If “Nvidia was knowingly doing business with companies tied to illegal chip sales and smuggling with China,” then “the Trump administration was asleep at the wheel,” she said.

“White House AI Czar David Sacks and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick were protecting their own fortunes rather than looking out for Americans,” Haworth remarked.

If the US fails to hold them accountable for alleged conflicts of interest, “it would send a signal that powerful men once again cannot be held to account and that powerful men are protecting powerful men,” Haworth remarked.

According to recent reports, detailing Sacks’ alleged conflicts, the group cited Latest York Times reporting that the former AI czar had long supported Huang’s stance that allowing Nvidia to sell more chips in China would help the US stay ahead in the AI race. After Sacks became Trump’s key AI advisor, Huang promptly forged a “tight bond” with him, and “both stood to benefit” from their push to sell chips to China, TOP reported.

In a recent development, also notably, while advising the White House, Sacks opposed policies such as the Trump administration’s recent move to cut off China’s remote access to US-made chips through now-restricted Southeast Asian data centers. Citing Sacks’ alignment with Huang, TOP reported that after just one meeting with the two men, Trump decided to allow Nvidia to sell AI chips to China that the Biden administration had previously blocked.

Huang valued his alliance with Sacks, TOP noted, citing reporting that demonstrated Huang declaring last year that Nvidia was “lucky” to have Sacks advising Trump. But TOP is concerned that the alliance was built on mutual financial interest and that Sacks took a part-time role in the Trump administration to avoid divestments or disclosure requirements that might have revealed the extent of his possible conflicts of interest.

TOP flagged two areas it believes warrant Congressional investigation. While advising Trump to embrace AI deregulation, Sacks and his firm, Craft Ventures, continued investing substantially in AI. Sacks also stood to benefit from pushing Trump to integrate AI into warfare and national security tools, TOP’s report noted. Craft Ventures has invested in Palantir, “a Peter Thiel-founded government contractor seen as a ‘rising star’ in the US Defense Tech World and holding hundreds of millions in US government defense contracts,” TOP said.

Even within the Trump administration, officials have turned on Commerce Secretary Lutnick, seemingly looking to blame him for mishandling the Nvidia spying investigation and allowing Trump to maintain close ties with Huang despite apparent intelligence risks.

Lutnick has bragged publicly that he promised Huang “really easy access to the President” after joining the administration, TOP reported. That alliance helped push Trump to approve the sale of Nvidia H200s to China, TOP said. And that seemed to directly benefit Lutnick, TOP said, because before he was confirmed as secretary, he was CEO of Cantor Fitzgerald, which held $1.2 billion in Nvidia stock.

“In his role as Secretary, Lutnick is responsible for policing exports of sensitive technology to adversaries and global rivals, like China,” TOP reported. “Lutnick and the organization he controls benefited greatly from opening sales of Nvidia chips to China.”.

After Lutnick was required to hand that tech giant over to his son, Cantor Fitzgerald “maintained extensive commercial ties to Nvidia, helping arrange billions of dollars in financing for companies in its AI business universe and repeatedly hosting its top executives,” TOP noted.

According to recent reports, those investments shifted substantially around the same time that Lutnick began facing pressure to “crack down on Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company suspected of funneling Nvidia’s advanced artificial intelligence chips to China,” TOP reported. Cantor Fitzgerald “reduced its Nvidia holdings by nearly 50 percent between September 2025 and March 2026,” TOP remarked.

However, when Trump was reportedly first told of the spying allegations this spring, Cantor Fitzgerald again continued to boost Nvidia. Most prominently, the firm helped “finance the expansion of one of Nvidia’s newest business partners, IREN,” facilitating a five-year, $3.4 billion deal between Nvidia and the Australia-based cloud computing provider.

Among those now criticizing Lutnick for weak enforcement of export controls that appeared designed to protect Huang’s bottom line is Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. But even with scrutiny coming from within the Trump administration, not everyone is convinced that Lutnick did anything wrong. Yoon suggested that, given Lutnick’s long career, there may be normal explanations for potential financial conflicts.

“Maybe a separate question is ‘should people with a long storied history in business and industry be working in government at this level?’” Yoon said.

Haworth remarked the next 48 hours will be critical in determining whether Huang succeeds in returning to Nvidia.

“I think it’s going to be incumbent on the incoming Democratic leadership to insist that whether or not he returns, investigations will follow,” Haworth noted.

But Yoon thinks Nvidia is unlikely to bring Huang back any time soon, despite current evidence suggesting that “Nvidia’s actions here have been perfectly legal” and that “influencing a political system for your financial interests is very much legal in the United States.”.

Sources indicate that it seems “untenable for Nvidia to continue doing what they’re doing,” Yoon remarked. Zooming out even more, he suggested the scandal highlighted that the entire AI industry can no longer afford to operate under a profit motive alone, so long as governments continue positioning the technology as a strategic asset.

If US investigations expose corruption, bribery, treason, or other crimes, Nvidia risks losing some of its dominant stake in the GPU market. On Tuesday, The Information reported that some Nvidia customers had already lost trust and were looking to Google and AMD for more stability.

Nvidia has also been accused of intervening in a Commerce investigation, which Yoon noted could also be “pretty consequential” if any evidence bears that out.

According to recent reports, “I think it’s pretty unlikely that Huang makes it back to Nvidia any time soon,” Yoon said. “Maybe he goes on a redemption tour and comes back in five years or something, but I’m not really seeing a path forward for him right now.”.

Copilot is "the new OS for work," and now Office runs inside of it

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Opening the keynote at its Ignite event, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella outlined the tech giant’s vision for its new “frontier ecosystem,” announcing Tuesday the general availability of Word, Excel, and PowerPoint inside Copilot, which he described as “the new OS for work.”.
  • The announcement is a striking inversion of how we’ve traditionally used software.
  • The rollout marks a major step toward the Copilot redesign the organization first announced in September.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Opening the keynote at its Ignite event, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella outlined the tech giant’s vision for its new “frontier ecosystem,” announcing Tuesday the general availability of Word, Excel, and PowerPoint inside Copilot, which he described as “the new OS for work.”.

The announcement is a striking inversion of how we’ve traditionally used software. Rather than an app like Word being the attraction and Clippy the assistant to help you use it, Microsoft envisions the latest Copilot integrations will see agents driving things, with the software packages riding shotgun. Applications will become plugin components of the agent’s work, backed by an organizational knowledge layer that draws context from emails, meetings, calendars, chats, and files. Users will now be able to create documents, spreadsheets, and presentations directly in Copilot, with the resulting files remaining editable in their respective Office applications.

The rollout marks a major step toward the Copilot redesign the organization first announced in September. Parts of that vision are now becoming “generally available,” as Nadella puts it, with autonomous agents and latest governance tools arriving alongside them.

Copilot Autopilot (not to be confused with Windows Autopilot) is a “persistent, proactive agent for personal productivity” according to Microsoft. In a nutshell, Autopilot is a cloud-based autonomous AI agent that users can delegate responsibilities to, not just single tasks. Autopilot can be authorized to work across services like email and calendars and complete tasks assigned to it as part of its role. Autopilot will use usage-based billing via Copilot Credits, but final pricing has not been confirmed ahead of general availability.

Also unveiled as generally available at the keynote speech was Microsoft IQ, an intelligence platform that houses Work IQ, a context layer that helps agents understand a manufacturer’s communications, relationships, and ongoing work. Nadella described Work IQ as perhaps a company’s most valuable database: “It has a deep understanding of the people, their relationships to other people, your emails, your meetings, chats, projects that make up all the fabric of work.” Whether companies want autonomous agents to have access to internal documents and messaging data will have to be determined by their own internal IT review.

Copilot Workspaces is a collaborative environment currently available through Microsoft’s Frontier early-access program, but coming soon will be the ability to bring personal Autopilot agents into Workspaces. Early in the keynote address, Nadella noted that “until now, AI interactions have mostly been single-player. Workspaces makes it a truly multiplayer experience, where people and agents drive towards a common goal, with shared context.”.

Trust, the third pillar of Microsoft’s upcoming frontier ecosystem, was something that Nadella continued returning to during his presentation, and not in a way that some might expect. “We find ourselves in a place where alignment is elusive. Mechanistic understanding of these models is elusive. The question is: How can you even trust all this powerful technology? The reality is, by definition, you can’t,” he mentioned.

Industry observers note that in a departure from the norms of “AI is magic” corporate hype sentiment, Nadella conceded that the internal workings of AI thought processes remain difficult to understand, and models cannot be trusted to govern themselves, regardless of whether their answers are accurate. Nadella described the solution as “an architectural imperative to separate the supply of intelligence” from the authority granted to it. Microsoft indicates each Autopilot agent will have a unique ID, and administrators can restrict permissions or block it entirely. All agent activities are logged for human review, and Autopilot can ask for human approval before engaging in certain actions.

In a recent development, the promised agent controls and admission that AI systems can’t always be trusted are meaningful, but Microsoft is asking businesses and owners to place their trust in the manufacturer’s own safeguards instead, though the effectiveness of those safeguards against mistakes, rogue actions, or data exposure must still be demonstrated. In Microsoft’s view, the solution to untrustworthy intelligence is not to make AI agents trustworthy, but to control what they’re permitted to do. Businesses will need to decide how much autonomy they delegate to agents.

Along with the guardrails, Microsoft announced what it calls the “AI Transparency Initiative.” The effort has partnered with 40-plus major companies, including Adobe and MasterCard, to develop open, industry-wide standards for AI governance and security. Nadella described the initiative as a way for industry to “help establish an open standard that makes AI safer, more transparent, and more accessible.”.

It has been revealed that along with the other confirmed additions, Microsoft also announced expanding capabilities for Agent 365, its existing control plane for managing AI agents across enterprise environments. The new agent sheriff extends existing identity, security, and management systems to AI agents. Microsoft describes the objective as providing “observability at every layer of the stack.” Agent 365 offers governance controls over agent behavior in what Microsoft says is “autonomous in execution, but bounded and supervised.”.

Sources indicate that along with Agent 365 comes Agent 365 Business Analytics: “You can simply think of this as an ERP system of AI usage. You can see exactly what’s driving the spend and connect the spend to the outcomes that drive business value,” said Nadella. Customers will be able to see real-world costs associated with AI token-spend and compare those metrics to the value of work performed. Microsoft acknowledged that the estimations of assisted work hours are determined by a model, and not a direct measurement of time that may have been saved. This is a telling concession for Microsoft to make as businesses evaluate whether there will be an ROI on AI implementations, but according to Judson Althoff, CEO of Microsoft Commercial Business, “anything you can do with Claude or ChatGPT, you can do better with Copilot, for less.”.

Nadella offered only a brief acknowledgment of last week’s outage that disrupted access to services like Exchange Online and Teams for users across the globe. “Last week was a reminder of how critical digital infrastructure is as the dial tone for the world,” he said. “We know the trust you place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously, and in that context I know we have work to do.”.

That statement was all the time the elephant in the room was given, but Microsoft did seem to acknowledge the public’s growing concern over data center projects by highlighting the previously discussed “community-first AI infrastructure initiative.” Not a surprise in a presentation that asks organizations to extend more autonomy to software agents, at a time when Microsoft’s existing infrastructure is under increased scrutiny.

Latest Update: What Is Pons? The Robinhood Chain Meme Coin Launchpad Explained

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1566 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Decrypt

💡 Key Takeaways
  • When Robinhood switched on its own Robinhood Chain blockchain on July 1, 2026, the trading app's stock tokens were supposed to be the main attraction.
  • Pons became the busiest place to make them.
  • In a recent development, that openness can also be exploited.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When Robinhood switched on its own Robinhood Chain blockchain on July 1, 2026, the trading app's stock tokens were supposed to be the main attraction. Instead, much of the early activity came from meme coins: tokens built around a joke or an internet trend.

Pons became the busiest place to make them. Like Pump.fun on Solana, it lets anyone pick a name, ticker and image and have a tradable token minutes later, without writing code. Its fees briefly made it one of the highest-earning protocols in crypto, and its own token, PONS, went on to list on Kraken and Coinbase.

In a recent development, that openness can also be exploited. In September 2026, an onchain analyst alleged that one group had used Pons introduces to extract millions of dollars from buyers.

This guide explains what Pons is, how its two generations of contracts work, what the PONS token does, and the risks.

Pons is a token launch protocol running on Robinhood Chain, a layer-2 network built on Ethereum using Arbitrum's technology, and its website and documentation are published by Pons Labs, LLC.

Every token rolled out through Pons is a standard ERC-20 token with a fixed supply, 1 billion tokens on V1 launches, that can never be increased. The creator gets no allocation set aside before trading opens.

According to recent reports, pons is also non-custodial. Its documentation notes every launch and trade is a transaction the user's own wallet signs, and the platform never holds user funds.

Pons went live within days of Robinhood Chain's mainnet. It picked up most of the chain's launchpad activity after an early rival, Noxa, stopped accepting newly introduced introduces on July 11, 2026, according to Decrypt's reporting.

Pons has two generations of contracts, V1 and V2, and both remain live on Robinhood Chain.

It has been revealed that in V1, a single transaction deploys the token and its trading pool, a Uniswap V3 pool paired with wrapped ETH (WETH), and locks the pool's liquidity so the creator can't withdraw it. Each launch costs 0.0005 ETH and carries a 1% trading fee, the documentation says. A launch "graduates" once 4.2 ETH has been paired in its pool by default, but trading carries on in the same pool.

V1 launches are protected for their first two blocks: in the launch block, only the creator's initial buy can execute, and for the rest of the window no wallet can hold more than 5% of supply or buy more than 5.5%. Fees are split 70% to the creator and 30% to the protocol for current launches.

V2 adds a bonding curve: a contract that holds a token's whole supply and sets its price by formula, rising as people buy and falling as they sell. According to the V2 documentation, the curve sells out, then "graduates" automatically into a Uniswap V4 pool, seeded with a fixed share of supply held back from the start. The pool's liquidity is then locked permanently; no unlock function exists.

V2 launches can be priced in ETH or in other assets Pons has approved, including tokenized stocks, in which case the creator is paid in that asset. Each trade pays a standard fee shared between Pons, the creator and an optional buyback, plus an optional creator tax that is capped by the protocol and fixed at launch.

When a creator turns buybacks on, part of their own fee is spent buying their token back. Those tokens are locked in a vault and released over five years, split between the creator and the protocol.

PONS itself was launched through Pons's own legacy V1 factory, and its documentation uses PONS as the reference token for developers testing their integrations.

Recent findings suggest that "Sniping" means buying a large share of a new token in its first seconds, often with bots, then selling into later buyers. Every V2 launch opens with a "snipe tax" of 99% on buys that decays to zero over five seconds, the documentation says.

The launching wallet and the creator's fee wallet are exempt automatically, and creators can name up to 32 more exempt addresses at launch "for a team bundling its opening buys across several wallets.".

Recent findings suggest that that exemption became central to allegations published on September 27, 2026. Pseudonymous onchain analyst Wazz tweeted that a single operation had extracted at least $18.43 million from 53 Robinhood Chain debuts between July 10 and September 21, 2026, mostly through Pons V2. Wazz said nearly every launch was sniped for 70% or more of its supply by bundles of 70 to 200 wallets.

I just uncovered the biggest serial Rugpulling and Extraction operation on Robinhood.

The same operation is linked 53 launches within a 2 month period.

Total Extracted: $18.43 MILLION.

1Password says the security breach didn’t compromise its vaults, but didn’t mention how many customers were affected.

In a recent development, if you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

According to recent reports, 1Password says a hacker stole customer names and email addresses after gaining access to its backend systems. The breach didn’t expose passwords or other information stored in customer vaults, but could put consumers at risk of phishing attempts, according to a post disclosing the incident. It’s unclear how many users are affected.

The password manager began investigating the incident on November 19th, after an attacker gained access to an employee’s corporate GitHub account. Using the compromised account, the hacker accessed 1Password’s source code and pushed malicious code to backend services to download customer data. Along with customer names and emails, the leaked data included public keys, as well as account and user identifiers.

In a recent development, it also included tokens from certain emailed invitation or account recovery links. According to 1Password, attackers can’t use tokens alone to gain access to an account, as they would need to pair them with a single-sign-on method or a six-digit numeric code sent to a user’s email. 1Password has since lengthened the codes it sends to owners to 10 alphanumeric characters to make them harder to guess.

In a recent development, the password manager also disabled the affected GitHub account, rotated internal credentials compromised by the breach, and added a fresh detection system for similar attacks. It warns customers about potential phishing attempts as well, saying phony emails, texts, or calls may reference 1Password invitations or account recovery attempts. The company claims it will never ask customers for their account password or Secret Key, and that owners should only enter this information into the official 1Password app or website.

According to recent reports, A lesser-known iOS 27 feature includes a new alarm volume setting that gives alarms, timers, and ringtones independent volume control. You can adjust the volume settings for alarms and timers independently of your phone’s alerts and system sounds, so you don’t miss an alarm after lowering your ringtone volume.

Also: Apple reveals daily limits on your Siri AI use – here’s how much you’ll have to pay.

There have been ways to adjust the iPhone alarm volume for a few years, but there’s an crucial distinction between what the newly introduced feature entails and what those methods involve.

Previously, you could adjust your Sleep Schedule alarms to always go off at a specific volume, regardless of the iPhone’s shared volume. Sleep Schedule alarms have a dedicated volume slider that you can set and adjust as needed, all configured within the Sleep focus. The latest feature, however, lets you set an independent volume for all alarms and timers, not just those in the Sleep Schedule.

Alarms, Timers, Alerts, and System Sounds are set to match your ringtone volume by default, but you can turn them off in the Sounds and Haptics setting.

Also: 5 upcoming Apple Health features you should try in iOS 27.3 – if your phone qualifies.

Once you disable the option to match your alarm volume to your ringtone’s volume, you can set your volume for upcoming alarms. With this feature, you can maximize your alarm volume without affecting the volume of incoming calls and notifications.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Microsoft saddles Windows 11 with hefty doses of two potential annoyances — AI and advertisements.
  • Industry observers note that you can try to ignore many of these, but they still get in your face.
  • Also: How to remove Copilot AI from Windows 11 completely – in 6 steps.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Microsoft saddles Windows 11 with hefty doses of two potential annoyances — AI and advertisements. The AI features include not just the Copilot app but AI in Notepad and Paint, Recall on Copilot+ PCs, and AI in Edge. As for ads, those typically come in the form of suggestions, tips, and promotions designed to tout other Microsoft products and services.

Industry observers note that you can try to ignore many of these, but they still get in your face. You can attempt to manually disable them, but that process can be challenging. Instead, I use a free third-party utility called Bloatynosy. This simple tool can deactivate a variety of annoyances and bloatware in Windows 11 across a range of categories.

Also: How to remove Copilot AI from Windows 11 completely – in 6 steps.

In a recent development, one category covers AI, another covers ads, a third focuses on privacy, and a fourth on installed apps. There are also categories for File Explorer, the taskbar, and Windows Patch. You’re able to explore each category to see the settings that can be removed or disabled.

Industry observers note that you can also run a check of your PC to see which features and settings are installed and active on your system. From there, just select the elements you want to eliminate, and the program will give them the heave-ho.

Now, here’s how you can use Bloatynosy to debloat your Windows 11 PC.

Bloatynosy is accessible through its GitHub page. Read the page to get the latest details on the program, and then click the button showing the release number. On the next page, you can choose between two variations of Bloatynosy. One is a plain version, while the other includes a Microsoft .NET 11 desktop runtime to spruce up the appearance of the software. I’d go with the .NET variation.

It has been revealed that extract the downloaded ZIP file. Dig through the resulting folders until you see the Bloatynosy.exe file. Right-click that file and run it as an administrator to launch the program; no installation required except for the .NET runtime if that component isn’t installed. If Microsoft Defender’s Smart Screen tries to prevent the app from opening, click the More info link and select the Run anyway button.

Industry observers note that the home screen for Bloatynosy displays all the categories for the different settings you may want to disable or remove. But your first task should be to check your PC to see which annoying elements are installed on your system. Click the Check PC button in the lower-right corner to start the scan.

According to recent reports, after the PC check has finished, Bloatynosy highlights you all the settings you can change or uninstall. Under AI, you may find settings to disable Copilot on the taskbar, disable the AI features in Edge, disable Recall, disable the AI features in Notepad and Paint, and remove Copilot entirely. Under ads, you’ll likely see options to disable Lock screen ads, disable Start menu ads, disable tailored experiences, disable tips and suggestions, and disable personalized ads.

Also: 4 Microsoft To Do app alternatives I’d try before it shuts down.

There are other helpful settings across other categories. You can align the Start button to the left, turn off the prompt to set Edge as the default browser, disable the Edge sign-in and first run experience (two settings I find particularly annoying), enable Dark mode, reduce the diagnostic data collected by Microsoft, and hide the Task View button on the taskbar.

Certain settings are checked by default, but you can opt to check or uncheck them all or just manually check specific ones. After you’ve confirmed or made your selections, click Apply if you want to run them.

Recent findings suggest that the results of the PC scan don’t display the settings in any specific order. For that reason, you might prefer to view and address them per category. Click the Home button to return to the Home screen. Click the Details button for any category you wish to explore. You can then select or deselect specific settings for that category. Click the Apply button to make those changes.

The screen then indicates how many settings were changed based on what you selected. It also notifies you if you need to restart File Explorer or Windows itself. After rebooting Windows, sign back in and reopen the program. Check the features and settings you removed or disabled to confirm that they’re gone.

What if you disable a setting and then want it back? No problem. Bloatynosy will restore it for you. In the program, run the PC check again, then return to a category where settings were changed. The modified settings will be grayed out. Select the ones you wish to reset and then click the Restore button. Those settings are restored to their previous values.

In a recent development, bloatynosy offers other options worth exploring. Right-click on a specific entry, and you can request more details about it, change just that one setting, select or deselect all the settings, or tell the program to ignore that entry in the future.

Finally, you’re able to adjust certain settings for the software. Click the Settings button at the top. Here, you can turn Dark mode on or off, enhancement the catalog of settings, and enable AI explanations. For that last option, you then must select an AI provider such as Grok, OpenAI, or Anthropic. You then have to request and enter an API key. After that, right-clicking an entry and requesting details on it lets you request an AI description of it.

Recent findings suggest that overall, Bloatynosy does an effective job of ridding Windows of bloatware and other annoyances. The program is simple and user-friendly, and I highly recommend it.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Saying it was necessary to prevent the possible spontaneous explosion of a stockpile of material used in igniters and blasting caps, the US Army conducted a controlled detonation of over 9,700 pounds of lead azide today at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP) in Middletown, Iowa.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hours after detonating 4.4 tons of lead azide in Iowa, officials reported early test results from the surrounding areas.

Hours after detonating 4.4 tons of lead azide in Iowa, officials reported early test results from the surrounding areas.

Saying it was necessary to prevent the possible spontaneous explosion of a stockpile of material used in igniters and blasting caps, the US Army conducted a controlled detonation of over 9,700 pounds of lead azide today at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP) in Middletown, Iowa. Videos of the detonation indicated plumes of smoke several hundred feet high drifting south before promptly dissipating.

Following the explosion, the Army confirmed that all of the barrels at the plant had been destroyed without any secondary explosions or infrastructure damage. “I believe, absolutely, that we reduced, as close to zero as it’s absolutely humanly possible, the risk to the health and safety of the people of Middletown and the extended communities throughout Iowa,” mentioned Maj. Gen. Eric Shirley during a press conference held two hours after the blast, according to the Associated Press.

Industry observers note that the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has been monitoring the area around the ammunition plant leading up to today’s event. According to a statement from the EPA following the detonation, “real-time air monitors are reporting zero detection of airborne lead throughout the region” an hour after the detonation. The data collected by EPA employees, contractors, and monitoring equipment is shared here.

The Army has used lead azide in munitions for nearly a century but began transitioning away from the material around 15 years ago because it can be difficult to transport and store. Over time, the material can degrade and crystallize and eventually become unstable enough to detonate at ambient temperatures. The Iowa ammunition plant housed 68 barrels containing about 9,700 pounds of lead azide, representing the country’s remaining stockpile. For safety reasons, the material was stored in liquid form embedded in sawdust and burlap bags while water and ethanol were added to prevent freezing. However, the decision was made to detonate the stockpile after an inspection by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms (ATF) discovered “significant crystallization on the exterior of the barrels” last March.

Ahead of today’s detonation, the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) supported a recommended, but voluntary, temporary relocation of all the residents of Middletown and immediate surrounding areas that began yesterday. A cone-shaped evacuation zone extends about five miles southwest of the ammunition plant to account for the post-explosion dispersion and deposition path of dust. Displaced residents will be lodged until Friday, November 27th, and can return home once the all-clear has been given.

To reduce the amount of lead dust released into surrounding areas and the environment, the Army stated it took several additional precautions as part of today’s detonation. Walls made of four 16,000-gallon water tanks were installed to capture lead particulate, while the aging earth-covered magazines holding the barrels were covered with tarps and lead containment screens and flooded with foam.

You can schedule WhatsApp texts you might forget to send up to two weeks ahead of time.﻿.

WhatsApp’s 3 billion users are getting an option that Meta says is one of the most requested features, with the ability to schedule messages in advance for both private conversations and group chats. Most messaging platforms have had this for a very long time, but now it’s on WhatsApp too.

If you think of a text at an inconvenient time or don’t want to forget to fire off a birthday message at 4AM, you can draft it and set it to send anywhere from 10 minutes to two weeks later. The feature works with photos and videos, too.

In a recent development, to schedule a message, press and hold the send button and pick the date and time you want it to arrive. It will look like any other message to the person receiving it. You can see all future messages you have lined up, and delete them beforehand if you change your mind.

Even if your phone is off or out of battery, your scheduled message will still show up at the time you chose, and it remains end-to-end encrypted like all your personal messages, so no one else can read it, not even us.

Scheduled messages work with text, photos and videos, and are rolling out globally over the coming weeks. It’s one more way to show up for the people who matter to you, now at exactly the right time.

Will Wright's next simulation will use AI to mine content from your memories

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The computer gaming world hasn’t heard much from Will Wright (SimCity, The Sims) since the underwhelming release of Spore in 2008 and Wright’s subsequent departure from Maxis owner EA.
  • MyMems, which is slated to release next year, differentiates itself from Wright’s previous projects by “turn[ing] the simulation inward,” as Wright’s Gallium Studios and partner Artificial Agency put it in a press release this morning.
  • “If my Grandmother ended up in a Grand Slam match against Serena Williams, who would win?” Wright says by way of example in the release.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The computer gaming world hasn’t heard much from Will Wright (SimCity, The Sims) since the underwhelming release of Spore in 2008 and Wright’s subsequent departure from Maxis owner EA. Now, well over 15 years later, Wright is starting to promote his next digital simulation, which will use generative AI technology to craft a game-like experience from players’ memories.

MyMems, which is slated to release next year, differentiates itself from Wright’s previous projects by “turn[ing] the simulation inward,” as Wright’s Gallium Studios and partner Artificial Agency put it in a press release this morning. The game will mine memories provided by the player to create digital people that can then form teams to solve puzzles in the game world.

“If my Grandmother ended up in a Grand Slam match against Serena Williams, who would win?” Wright says by way of example in the release. “If I had to build a bridge across a short chasm, which three people from my life would I choose to help me?”.

Sources indicate that in an accompanying announcement video, Wright talks about how the “plausible behavior” in a game like The Sims still didn’t effectively capture the nuances of people he encounters in real life. “It was nowhere near them understanding my claustrophobia or why my sister and I fought so much… We’re actually taking parts of your life, your memories, your experiences, people you know, and turning that into a game that’s very personal.”.

Wright said MyMems will be able to extract generalized themes from your memories into self-contained areas that Wright compared to the various parts in a theme park: Sports, vacations, injuries, memories, and deaths could all be the basis for their own zones to play in. Players will also have the option to create worlds based on shared memories with family, friends, and co-workers, for example.

Sources indicate that since this is 2026, it shouldn’t be surprising that MyMems is making heavy use of generative AI (with a “proprietary behavior engine” on top) to transform your typed-up memories into simulated locales and characters. In the announcement video, Wright praises the “entirely open-ended” AI systems Gallium is using “to extract from the stories and whatnot based upon the memories you put into the game.”.

In a recent development, but Wright’s focus on mining memories for simulation content predates the current generative AI boom. What has now become MyMems started off as Proxi, a mobile simulation that was first unveiled in 2018 as “a game of self-discovery, a game where we actually uncover the hidden you.” But after years of pre-production work (as outlined in an excellent Vulture piece earlier this year), Wright’s Gallium Studios finally ran out of funding in late 2024, leading to mass layoffs for the small team and an uncertain future for the project.

Now the idea has been revived thanks in large part to a partnership with AI middleware firm Artificial Agency. Until now, that company has mainly been focused on agentic systems that can create “virtual players” to playtest a game or serve as a partner for human players.

Now, Artificial Agency’s marketing claims the tech giant’s AI tool will be used to create “a personal behavior model and a knowledge graph” from players’ memories, drawing some unsettling comparisons to big tech surveillance.

Industry observers note that “Meta knows what you click,” the company writes. “Netflix knows what you watch. Nobody knows what you remember. MemDNA learns from your memories locally and only with your permission.”.

Recent findings suggest that wright stated the partnership with Artificial Agency will let Gallium benefit from “off-the-shelf” AI solutions without having to “become an AI research firm” in its own right. He also said the collaboration will help limit costs by providing a cheaper option than the “really expensive” frontier models that might be overkill for a project like this.

“Right now AI has opened a vast new design area and I’m enjoying, you know, exploring that as a designer,” Wright remarked.

Whether they’re your kindred spirit or the person you live vicariously through, one thing never changes: They always need newly introduced gear.

That’s what makes travelers so fun to buy for. But you don’t want to get them just anything. The key is to find that clever gift even they didn’t know they needed, and that’s where we come in. From streaming gadgets for the hotel to portable espresso makers and high-capacity chargers, these are our favorite gifts to help travelers take their next adventure to the next level.

Give Yourself A Gift With Holiday Travel Deals. Make the most of the season with limited-time holiday offers on travel and more. However you choose to celebrate, explore more ways to save and make your next journey even more rewarding. Terms apply. Ends December 15, 2026.

Every traveler needs a go-to backpack, and the Uniqlo Utility stands out for all the little things. Its minimalist, water-resistant design hides plenty of pockets on the front and sides, plus a roomy laptop sleeve and extras, including a handy key holder in the front pocket.

Few things are more frustrating on a long flight than trying to keep your phone stable between your seasoned pretzels and fellow passengers. Thankfully, MiiKare’s adjustable, inexpensive clamp can make things less stressful for your favorite frequent flyer, so they can finally watch Olympus Has Fallen in peace.

We all tend to skimp on simple items for ourselves, which is why this fancy-pants sleep mask makes such a thoughtful present. Its 3D contoured fit is designed to block all light while providing plush memory foam comfort so your loved one can get the rest they need between adventures.

It has been revealed that for frequent flyers, a plain suitcase sticker may not be enough. In the age of QR codes, Pebblebee’s Link Bag Tags make a lot more sense. They’re battery-free, scannable by anyone with a phone, and offer built-in privacy with the ability to share or deny personal information.

They say once you go bidet, you never go back. That’s certainly harder to achieve when traveling outside Japan, though Tushy offers an effective solution with its handy, collapsible bidet. The manual contraption isn’t heated, but one portable bathroom luxury at a time.

It has been revealed that mechanism’s clever, durable creations are a favorite here at The Verge. The company’s foldable tray table mount is particularly brilliant, offering travelers an ergonomic way to mount devices — including larger gaming handhelds like the Steam Deck — for easy access on long flights. Just don’t forget to pick up the proper grip.

Built for jet setters, Anker’s 100W travel adapter features a durable design, a handy LCD display to track charge percentage, and compatibility in over 200 countries. It doesn’t support AC plugs, but it does have four USB inputs for all your portables, including a trio of USB-C ports.

What if you could give the gift of stress-free Wi-Fi on the go? That’s the promise of TP-Link’s dual-band Roam 7, a portable Wi-Fi 7 router that simplifies connecting to public portals so travelers can connect everything to a single device and be done with it.

According to recent reports, for the fastidious person on your list who can’t stop polishing their camera, tablet, or other delicate piece of equipment, there’s the lightweight Magic Wrap. The foldable, plush fabric sticks to itself, with no zippers, edges, or even magnets to scuff or scratch your most precious gear.

It has been revealed that you can’t project anything anywhere from your phone or watch (yet), but the Aurzen Zip makes that moment feel closer. Bright and durable, the foldable projector can mirror content from your phone or tablet on most flat surfaces, but fair warning: It doesn’t work with streaming services like Netflix without a $129.99 CastPlay HDMI dongle.

Whether your favorite traveler is a packing nerd or a slob who’s always losing everything (we’re not here to judge), everyone can use a little extra organization. Cocoon’s Grid-It accessories store it all, from chargers and gadgets to makeup and passports, with flexible straps to lock it all in.

According to recent reports, losing crucial documents on a trip can be disastrous. Bagsmart’s Blast Travel Pouch is a great way to keep them all safe, with multiple pockets, an easily adjustable strap, and even RFID blocking to deflect electronic thieves.

It’s time for a smarter robovac. Thankfully, there’s the Matic, which looks less like the rambling discs that pervade the space and more like an actual robot that, well, vacuums. It doesn’t get under beds, but it also doesn’t get stuck under them, and it does a great job providing truly no-fuss cleaning thanks to its superb mapping.

Industry observers note that one charging port, two phones. That’s not a problem with Anker’s dual-headed USB-C cable, which offers either 4 or 6 feet of length to provide game-changing versatility when you need it most.

Who claims you can’t travel with a big screen? The Xreal One Pro feature dual micro-OLED displays to project a virtual 171-inch screen from your device of choice. A 57-degree field of view, max 120Hz refresh rate, and built-in speakers round things out, delivering portable cinematic entertainment for one.

Apple’s AirPods Pro are the epitome of wireless earbud refinement, with fantastic noise-canceling and transparency modes, a light and airy fit, and clear sound thanks to ear tips that seal your ears without plugging them up. The latest pair continues the quest for perfection with faster processing, more features, and better ergonomics than ever.

Industry observers note that oura didn’t reinvent the wheel with the Ring 5, but it did reshape it into a slimmer, thinner, more wearable design that could make all the difference. Inside are the same extensive health and fitness-tracking features for charting everything from sleep to heart health, backed by long battery life.

According to recent reports, whether you’re white-water rafting or trekking through a damp jungle, keeping your gear dry is essential. The Sea to Summit dry bag is a slick, affordable solution with clever features, including a reflective interior and a D-ring buckle to secure it to boats and bikes. The solid warranty is just a plus.

SwitchBot’s powerful, battery-powered fan is a big upgrade over your average plug-in. As a 3D circulator, it can tilt to push air in all directions. You can also control it via an app, and it even detaches from its stand to sit on a desk or tabletop. Quiet and versatile, it’s equipped for nearly any adventure on or off the grid.

According to recent reports, espresso in the woods? Yes, please. The GR2’s magical mechanics make it possible, letting you turn 12 ounces of grounds into espresso without power. Its carrying case houses all the accessories needed to get that sweet shot of bean, making real coffee available virtually anywhere.

Theragun’s latest therapeutic cure for sore muscles is as packable as it is luxurious. The third-gen Mini includes clever features like a travel lock to keep it off during transport, guided routines, and USB-C charging. There’s even a Y2K edition for the ’90s kid in all of us.

It has been revealed that for travelers hitting the road when the thermometer is rising, cooling off is essential. Nitecore’s long-lasting izzCool 10 Pro offers heat relief with a powerful fan and fillable reservoir that mists you for a refreshing respite from the sun. It even works with larger containers to double as a nighttime humidifier.

Every traveler needs quality noise-canceling for long flights, but flagship headphones are becoming increasingly spendy. Sony’s former flagship WH-1000XM4 were so good, they’ve been bestsellers through two latest generations. Now the company has revamped them in the XM4C, adding minor improvements to a stone-cold classic at a nice price.

In a recent development, packing light is essential for all travelers, but it’s particularly vital for those who trek long distances. This high-capacity Nitecore charger is a killer addition to any pack, with water resistance, fast charging, and a slim, lightweight design that can power your devices without weighing them down.

Industry observers note that the Switch 2 leverages the same ideas as its predecessor, only with a larger, 7.9-inch display, a faster chip, and a bevy of new social features. However, its most key trait is that it’s the newest Nintendo console, which means access to a host of weird, beautiful, family-friendly games that only Nintendo could dream up, now on a better screen.

Fortunately, Tessan’s pack-friendly power strip offers all the ports, with multiple USB-C, USB-A, and AC inputs to charge everything in one place.

It has been revealed that if you have an avid road tripper on your list, Ugreen’s four-port car charger blends slick design with serious utility. More importantly, it has a built-in retractable USB-C cable that delivers up to 60W of power and keeps things tidy.

For on-the-go creators, it’s all about capturing the moment in the highest video quality possible. Buying your loved one a pair of shoes is tougher than you might think, but a gift card to The Walking Company is a step in the right direction. The store offers a wide variety of ultra-comfortable kicks, boots, sandals, and even orthotics, along with a shoe finder to help them find the right fit.

According to recent reports, retroid has had its stumbles, but the Pocket 5 is a hit, making it a great gift for the globe-trotting gamer. Recent findings suggest that newly introduced parents need everything, all at once, and traveling always raises the stakes. Offering 10 soothing sounds from a crazy-compact frame with up to 15 hours of juice, it’s simple, effective, and essential.

How is your giftee supposed to bring you back something special when they’re already overpacked? The Matador Packable Duffel, of course. The durable, 30-liter carrier breaks down to micro size, then easily expands to hold loads of overseas paraphernalia. It’s a win-win!

Muse privacy invasions are freaking out Meta staffers, internal chats show

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1581 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • After some early adopters of Meta’s Muse AI agent complained that it was spying on private messages and behaving unpredictably earlier this fall, Reuters exposed internal chats showing that Meta staff had raised the same alarms.
  • When testing the agent, staff warned that Muse appeared to be accessing encrypted private messages that users did not expect the bot to review, could be mixing up conversations between users, and even potentially sharing sensitive information users would never expect to be exposed.
  • Some unexpected Muse outputs responded to questions that staffers never asked.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After some early adopters of Meta’s Muse AI agent complained that it was spying on private messages and behaving unpredictably earlier this fall, Reuters exposed internal chats showing that Meta staff had raised the same alarms.

When testing the agent, staff warned that Muse appeared to be accessing encrypted private messages that users did not expect the bot to review, could be mixing up conversations between users, and even potentially sharing sensitive information users would never expect to be exposed.

Some unexpected Muse outputs responded to questions that staffers never asked.

“Hmmm,” one Meta staffer wrote in an instance where Muse sent the definition of “money laundering” unbidden. “Got a random ping from Muse about something I definitely did not ask for… .”.

In at least one case, Muse told a staffer surprised by a similarly out-of-context offer to message a seller about a coffee table that it had “pulled in some context about a coffee table pickup that doesn’t seem to be yours.”.

According to Reuters, that employee flagged the troubling output, writing, “this was ‘not my conversation’” and “expressing concern about a ‘possible cross-account context leak.’”.

It has been revealed that raising the most concern were random outputs that appeared to share private user data. For example, a perplexed Meta staffer chatting with Muse about fishing got a random extra response, seemingly sharing balances from two unknown bank accounts. That output said, “BTW, two bank updates, your Capital One balance is $2722.58, your Charles Schwab balance is $5899.57.”.

According to recent reports, at least one staffer noted they lost money testing Muse, Reuters reported. That staffer reported that Muse “accidentally rolled me into a premium insurance proposal” for their dog that charged them $888 per month instead of their prior rate of $200. “Couldn’t recover,” the staffer said.

Meta’s spokesperson, Daniel Roberts, told Reuters that these were “isolated incidents,” and internally employees were told that “the agent appeared to be hallucinating messages in response to built-in prompts pushing it to engage with people in between sessions.” In those cases, an AI team member remarked the hallucinations were “unfortunately” biased “towards the most uncomfortable topics, like finances/security/safety, which sucks.” In some cases, instead of bank details, Muse hallucinated bitcoin balances, the team member said.

According to recent reports, A Meta spokesperson told Ars that “employee testing is core to the product development process and the entire point is to get feedback, so we can implement safety and privacy protections and improve products. Importantly, employees have access to different versions of Muse than the public, so they’re often reviewing features, functionality, and behavior not available elsewhere.”.

Speaking to Reuters, Roberts reiterated that “many of the messages flagged by employees as potential account mix-ups were hallucinations” that Meta had already addressed.

But Roberts declined to respond to Reuters’ questions on the prevalence or persistence of the issues the AI team member discussed. And Reuters’ report emphasized that the outlet independently was “unable to establish whether Muse was giving owners other people’s bank account balances and other sensitive data, or making up the information.”.

In a recent development, meta started receiving privacy-related complaints from Muse users in September. An Inc. Magazine reporter, Jason Aten, was shocked when it became clear that Muse was digging through private messages on his Mac without permission, reporting that he instead “explicitly” chose to deny Muse that access. As Meta delayed responding, the agent claimed it was simply parsing text in push notifications, but Aten found that “wasn’t true.” Rather, the agent was syncing messages from a local database, which Aten said was activated without his knowledge.

Recent findings suggest that eventually, a Meta spokesperson, David Singleton, responded to Aten on social media. Singleton insisted that Aten must have opted into granting “macOS system-level Full Disk Access” with the “Messages connector” enabled, if Muse was reading his private messages.

But Aten said the response wasn’t good enough.

“Email me, David,” Aten responded. “Full Disk Access off. Muse synced 187k lines from my messages chat [database]. Something’s not great. Also, that Full Disk Access doesn’t say anything about your message database, and I specifically gave Muse a goal that had nothing to do with messages, so it had no business doing that even if I had given it permission.”.

Around the same time, Singleton responded to another user warning that his Muse appeared to be hacked. In that case, the user remarked that Muse tried to access an email service after claiming the user asked it to.

“I didn’t even open the app today at all,” the user wrote, vowing to delete the app and report it to Apple. “This is crazy.”.

In a lengthy response providing more technical details, Singleton confirmed that Meta had received “a few reports” of such cases “where people thought their Muse was hallucinating or leaking other people’s data.” As he explained, the challenges arose after Meta deployed an revision giving Muse instructions on “how to engage with the user and ask them for confirmation before taking specific actions.”.

Sources indicate that it seems those instructions “landed on every message, not just messages pertaining to those specific actions, so its impact was wider than intended,” Singleton said. Also: “the way this instruction was provided to the model was done in a way that the model was not expecting (i.e. was not trained to expect).”.

Recent findings suggest that “We investigated with urgency and determined that this was caused by a bug introduced in the product that caused the model to hallucinate and was NOT a security or privacy concern,” Singleton wrote. “The bug has now been fixed.”.

Aten warned that even though you can’t rely on Muse to explain its own behavior, the agent’s response coupled with Meta’s did little to rebuild trust after the shocking intrusion into his private messages.

Recent findings suggest that “If we grant Singleton’s premise that I managed to unknowingly click something that enabled this capability, I still think that’s really bad,” Aten wrote. “You should not design your system in a way that people end up surprised by this kind of thing.” And if you do, you should not make “user control the central pitch” for marketing Muse, Aten suggested.

“If an AI agent is going to read my private messages, there should be a moment when it clearly asks me whether that’s okay,” Aten wrote.

Since Muse rolled out in September, it has been downloaded more than 10 million times, tapping Meta’s vast user network to quickly become one of the most-used AI agent tools.

According to recent reports, but staffers warned Meta that consumers may be blindsided by some actions the agents take, depending on the operating system the app is connected to. For example, one staffer was surprised to find that “Muse was set up by default with permission to access push notifications on phones with Google’s Android operating system.” That, too, gave access to private message preview text the staffer had not intended for the agent’s review.

Meta says that Muse customers can trust the firm to keep their data private. It also warns users that Muse can make mistakes, while building into its terms that users are responsible for actions taken by Muse (like maybe buying things you don’t want or making doctor’s appointments you don’t need). The tech giant said it’s continuously updating user protections, conducting internal testing, and prioritizing user safety.

However, Reuters worked with staff at Signal and the AI Now Institute to test if they could replicate that Meta staffer’s and others’ Muse experiences. On Android devices, they found that Muse could read Signal messages by bypassing Meta’s “Connector” tool and instead relying on permissions granted during initial setup.

In a recent development, on iPhone, requests were blocked, Reuters reported. But on Apple’s macOS, Muse repurposed “settings Apple offers to help people with disabilities operate their computers” to retrieve messages, including screenshot tools.

In a recent development, that testing “indicated the concern described by the Meta employees was ongoing and could be affecting others,” Reuters reported. Overall, Meta seemed to be interpreting permissions from Muse consumers “broadly,” Reuters concluded, in ways that privacy advocates and regulators may disagree with.

Signal President Meredith Whittaker told Reuters that Meta launched Muse “without showing any respect for basic privacy or cybersecurity.” She demanded that Meta make changes to give app developers like Signal “consistent technical ways” to “mark their applications as off-limits to AI agents,” Reuters reported.

Part of that change would require operating systems to enforce rules that app developers set to rope off AI agents from sensitive data, Whittaker suggested. And following Reuters’ reporting, both Apple and Google are already weighing potential changes to “give people more control over what they authorize with AI agents.”.

Apple, in particular, seemed disturbed by how Muse may be manipulating accessibility tools for people with disabilities. In October, Apple had already announced changes coming in response to consumers complaining about Muse accessing private messages without their knowledge or explicit consent. At that time, Apple concluded that “some developers were using the Full Disk Access feature in ways that could put users at risk.” And they promised to “introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access can only do so with very explicit user action.”.

“We are committed to ensuring owners understand exactly what they are allowing, so they can make informed choices about their data and privacy,” Apple remarked.
